fibre.sample: stratified sample of 83 of 363 ready-to-wear styles (80 proportional by category + 3 denim added after the denim path was found outside /ready-to-wear/); census

craft_evidence.owned: Paris atelier stated (60 people, longest-serving petite main 30 years) — a claim with figures, no named place or photograph of a making facility; no factory ownership stated
craft_evidence.makers: none — 0 of 83 sampled product pages name a maker
craft_evidence.mills: none — 0 of 83 sampled pages name a mill
craft_evidence.madein: 0 of 83 sampled product pages state a country
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed — Gaby Aghion, Paris, first collection in the 1950s (1952), year-by-year history page
craft_evidence.process: partial — atelier page gives runway-making figures (hours per bespoke dress, metres of silk); nothing on how the retail range is made
craft_evidence.reasoning: The heritage is dated and placed (Aghion, Paris, 1952) and the atelier page puts numbers on a Paris couture-style workroom, but nothing names where the sold range is made: no country, maker or mill appears on any of 83 sampled product pages. A house history and a runway atelier are not verifiable making for the range; 2 on the heritage alone.
